title: Discovering a Server and Negotiating What It Can Do

questions.question: A client wants a server's identity, supported protocol versions, and capabilities in a single round trip before it sends anything else. Which request gives it all three together?
options: resources/list, which returns the server's readable resources and their URIs
server/discover, which returns supported versions, capabilities, and identity together
prompts/list, which returns the reusable templates a user can select
the initialize handshake, which a connection completes before any request
questions.explanation: server/discover is the single request built for this: its DiscoverResult carries supportedVersions, capabilities, and the server's self-reported identity together, and the 2026-07-28 revision removed the initialize handshake entirely.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes when server/discover must be implemented and when it must be called?
options: Neither side is required to support it, since it is purely experimental tooling
Clients must call it before any other request, and servers may skip implementing it
Servers must implement it, and clients may call it or skip it entirely
Both sides must implement it and call it exactly once per connection
questions.explanation: The specification requires every server to implement server/discover, but calling it is optional for a client, which may send any request directly and handle a version error if one comes back.

questions.question: A tools/call request omits the elicitation capability from clientCapabilities, but the tool being called needs it to ask a follow-up question mid call. What does a conformant server do?
options: It proceeds anyway and silently skips the follow-up question to stay fast
It returns a tools/call error -32602 because the arguments fail the input schema
It queues the call and waits for the client to reconnect with elicitation enabled
It returns MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError, code -32021, naming exactly which capability the request lacked
questions.explanation: A server must not rely on a capability the client did not declare on that request, so it returns -32021 with data.requiredCapabilities naming exactly what the client needs to declare before retrying.

questions.question: A client sends a request naming an older protocol version to a server whose supportedVersions list does not include it. What should the client do next?
options: Retry the same request with a version taken from the error data
Treat the server as unreachable and stop sending it any further requests
Fall back to the initialize handshake from the earlier revision
Resend the identical request unchanged, since the server retries automatically
questions.explanation: UnsupportedProtocolVersionError carries data.supported and data.requested, and the client should retry the request with a new id using a version from data.supported rather than assuming the server is legacy or unreachable.

questions.question: A client discovers that a server offers tools with listChanged notifications, then later sends a tools/call request. Which capabilities may the server rely on when handling that specific call?
options: The union of every clientCapabilities value the client has ever declared
Only the clientCapabilities included in that request's own _meta, checked fresh
Whatever the server advertised in its own DiscoverResult earlier in the exchange
Whatever capabilities the client declared on its very first request to it
questions.explanation: Servers must not infer capabilities from prior requests, even on the same connection, so a server can only rely on the clientCapabilities declared in the _meta of the request it is currently handling.

questions.question: A DiscoverResult's _meta carries io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo with the server's self-reported name and version. What is this field appropriate for?
options: Selecting which OAuth scopes the client requests from the authorization server
Deciding whether to grant the server elevated tool permissions
Display, logging, and debugging, never a security or authorization decision
Authenticating the server before the client sends its first real request
questions.explanation: serverInfo is self-reported and unverified by the protocol, so the specification says to use it for display, logging, and debugging only, never for security or authorization decisions.
